source.title: On Suppressing Range of Adaptive Stepsizes of Adam to Improve Generalisation Performance

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper. Table I's flattened layout does not reliably assign its values to methods, so those values are not extracted.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares Adam and momentum SGD on held-out validation performance across language and image tasks, using its own optimizer experiments rather than reproducing the original comparison method.
record.gate_note: Rows record Adam and SGD comparator results relevant to V4. SET-Adam and other new optimizer comparisons are not extracted as claim results. Table I's flattened transformer values are not assigned to methods; WGAN-GP FID is not a held-out generalization measure for V4.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own Adam-versus-momentum-SGD validation comparisons on language and image tasks, bearing on V4. Its tuning includes epsilon searches, so it does not reproduce the learning-rate-and-schedule-only restriction.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that SET-Adam's suppression of adaptive-stepsize range improves performance across their tested tasks, outperforming the eight adaptive baselines on language and CIFAR classification, matching the best adaptive performance on WGAN-GP, and exceeding Adam and AdaBelief on ImageNet. They describe momentum SGD as performing well mainly on image classification.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces SET-Adam, which modifies Adam's second-moment values through layerwise down-scaling, ϵ-embedding, and down-translating; compares optimizer validation performance across NLP, image classification, and image generation tasks.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture change whether Adam or SGD has better validation performance in the reported LSTM and CIFAR comparisons. Optimizer hyperparameters are searched over discrete sets for validation performance.

fits_no_version.finding: On ImageNet ResNet18, Adam has higher training accuracy but lower validation accuracy than SET-Adam; validation accuracies are 69.03% and 69.77%, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Modifying Adam's adaptive stepsizes with SET-Adam can improve validation performance despite lower training accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: WGAN-GP optimizers differ in best FID, selected across hyperparameters and repetitions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects generated-image quality; this does not measure the held-out generalization comparison named by V4.

record.peer_reviewed: ECML/PKDD (as stated in the supplied metadata)
record.problems: The paper's main experimental comparisons evaluate SET-Adam against baselines rather than systematically testing V4's limited-tuning claim. Hyperparameters are selected using validation performance, so the comparisons reflect the reported tuning procedure. Table I's flattened values cannot be assigned reliably. Table III's CIFAR100 ResNet34 validation-accuracy entries for SGD and Adam appear anomalous as supplied.
record.rows_left_out: Table I transformer results were omitted because the flattened text does not reliably assign values to methods. Table III results for other optimizers were omitted because they are not Adam or SGD outcomes needed for V4. WGAN-GP FID results were omitted because they do not report held-out generalization performance. No numeric SGD comparison is stated for ImageNet.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

The exact learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning restriction; a controlled limited-versus-broader-tuning comparison; recovery specifically attributable to decoupled weight decay or switching to SGD; equal or better training performance for Adam in the reported SGD comparisons.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Removing memorized versus random training examples.

missing.what: Add the explicit qualitative transformer Adam-versus-SGD result. Numeric Table I omission is declared, but the reliable prose comparison can still be recorded: SGD is inferior to every adaptive method except Fromage and MSVAG, including Adam.
missing.locator: Section III-A, final paragraph; Table VII for tuning; 400-epoch budget

record.verdict_notes: Both rows of each Adam/SGD pair must use the same claim-relative state; they are duplicate representations of one comparison. Table III is recoverable from the supplied text: Adam's ResNet34 accuracies are 95.09±0.18 on CIFAR10 and 77.31±0.14 on CIFAR100. Epsilon searches broaden tuning beyond V4's restricted protocol, but the paper does not isolate the causal effect of broader tuning. No original-source exclusion applies.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold and test error across widths.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

The paper does not test Wilson et al.'s limited-tuning comparison as a general claim across benchmarks; it tunes optimizer parameters on its own tasks. It does not test broader tuning, decoupled weight decay as a recovery, or switching from Adam to SGD.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
